To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inhibition of lapatinib-induced transcriptional reprogramming in ERBB2-positive breast cancer by targeting BET family bromodomains prevents the development of lapatinib resistance.
the kinome reprogrammed by lapatinib can be targeted by inhibiting the BET family chromatin reader proteins.
BET bromodomain inhibitors suppress the kinome response to lapatinibu, thereby overcoming the challenge of heterogeneity in kinome adaptation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new therapeutic targets and the development of new therapeutic agents.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies to overcome drug resistance in breast cancer, and in particular, to overcome resistance to the HER2-targeted drug lapatinib.
the development of a novel therapeutic approach to target the kinome in cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adaptive kinome responses to single kinase inhibitors are themselves a targetable Achilles heel, and targeting chromatin readers may be a generalizable strategy for overcoming resistance to single kinase inhibitors.

the combination therapy of lapatinib and bromodomain inhibitors is effective against breast cancer cells that have become resistant to lapatinib alone, and the combination therapy is also effective against cells that have become lapatinib resistant by expressing the mutant form of the ERBB2 protein, HER2-1047ins.
the combination of BET bromodimain inhibitors with lapatinib prevents kinome adaptation in ERBB2-positive breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BET bromodomain inhibitors are a potential therapeutic approach to prevent the development of resistance to ERBB2-targeted therapies.
BET inhibitors are able to block kinome reprogramming in lapatinib-resistant ERBB2+ breast cancer by blocking transcription.
BET bromodomain inhibitors are a promising strategy for overcoming lapatinib resistance by preventing the kinome response to lapatinub.
The main takeaway from our work is that
targeting the adaptive kinome itself is critical for durable responses to single kinase inhibitors.
the adaptive kinome reprogrammed in response to a kinase inhibitor is itself a target for therapeutic intervention.

the adaptive kinome responses to targeted therapies are not static but are highly plastic and can be inhibited by targeting chromatin readers, which in turn prevents reprogramming of the tumor kinome.
